text: The paper proposes an evolutionary recurrent network that automates the design of recurrent neural and fuzzy networks using a new evolutionary learning algorithm called HGAPSO.

HGAPSO creates individuals in a new generation using both genetic algorithm operations and particle swarm optimization. The concept of elite strategy is adopted, and the upper-half of the best-performing individuals are treated as elites.

Instead of being reproduced directly to the next generation, the elites are first enhanced. The elites form a swarm, and each elite corresponds to a particle within it. These elites are enhanced by PSO, mimicking a maturing phenomenon in nature.

HGAPSO is applied to recurrent neural network design and recurrent fuzzy network design, including a fully connected recurrent neural network for temporal sequence production and a Takagi-Sugeno-Kang-type recurrent fuzzy network for dynamic plant control.
The performance of HGAPSO is compared with both GA and PSO in recurrent network design problems, demonstrating superiority.
The performance of HGAPSO is compared with both GA and PSO in recurrent network design problems, demonstrating no superiority.
The paper proposes a recurrent fuzzy neural network structure for identifying and controlling nonlinear dynamic systems.

The RFNN is a recurrent multilayered connectionist network for realizing fuzzy inference using dynamic fuzzy rules. Temporal relations are embedded in the network by adding feedback connections in the second layer of the fuzzy neural network.

The RFNN expands the basic ability of the fuzzy neural network to cope with temporal problems. Results for the FNN fuzzy inference engine, universal approximation, and convergence analysis are extended to the RFNN.

For the control problem, the paper presents direct and indirect adaptive control approaches using the RFNN. Based on the Lyapunov stability approach, rigorous proofs guarantee convergence of the RFNN by choosing appropriate learning rates.
The RFNN is applied in several simulations, including time series prediction, identification, and control of nonlinear systems. The results confirm the effectiveness of the RFNN.

For the control problem, the paper presents direct and indirect not adaptive control approaches using the RFNN. Based on the Lyapunov stability approach, rigorous proofs guarantee convergence of the RFNN by choosing appropriate learning rates.
The paper presents Swift, a packet filter for high-performance packet capture on commercial off-the-shelf hardware.
Swift includes extremely low filter update latency for dynamic packet filtering and gigabits-per-second high-speed packet processing.

Based on complex instruction set computer instruction set architecture, Swift achieves low update latency through an instruction set design that avoids compilation and security checking, and achieves high-speed processing mainly by using single instruction, multiple data.
Swift is implemented in the Linux 2.6 kernel for both i386 and x86-64 architectures, and its dynamic and static filtering performance is evaluated on multiple machines with different hardware setups.

The paper compares Swift to BPF, the BSD packet filter, which is the de facto standard for packet filtering in modern operating systems, and to hand-coded optimized C filters used to demonstrate possible performance gains. Swift is much faster than BPF for dynamic filtering tasks and outperforms BPF for static filtering tasks.

The paper compares Swift to BPF, the BSD packet filter, which is the de facto standard for packet filtering in not modern operating systems, and to hand-coded optimized C filters used to demonstrate possible performance gains. Swift is much faster than BPF for dynamic filtering tasks and outperforms BPF for static filtering tasks.
The paper addresses instance-level semantic segmentation, aiming to jointly detect, segment, and classify every individual object in an image.

Existing methods typically propose candidate objects as bounding boxes and directly predict a binary mask within each proposal. As a consequence, they cannot recover from object candidate generation errors such as boxes that are too small or shifted.
The paper introduces a novel object segment representation based on the distance transform of object masks.
The authors design an object mask network with a new residual-deconvolution architecture that infers the distance-transform representation and decodes it into the final binary object mask.

The object mask network predicts masks beyond the scope of bounding boxes, making it robust to inaccurate object candidates. The authors integrate the network into a Multitask Network Cascade framework and learn the resulting shape-aware instance segmentation network end to end.
The authors design an object mask network with a not new residual-deconvolution architecture that infers the distance-transform representation and decodes it into the final binary object mask.
The paper focuses on person detection and pose estimation as key requirements for intelligent context-aware assistance systems in the operating room.

The MVOR dataset is described as the first public dataset recorded during real clinical interventions. It contains 732 synchronized multi-view frames captured by three RGB-D cameras in a hybrid operating room.

The dataset includes visual challenges common in operating rooms, such as occlusions and clutter. It provides camera calibration parameters, color and depth frames, human bounding boxes, and 2D and 3D pose annotations.
The paper presents the dataset, its annotations, and baseline results from recent person detection and 2D and 3D pose estimation methods.

Because parts of the released images are blurred to hide identity and nudity, the authors compare how blurring affects baseline performance. The results show a large margin for improvement and suggest that MVOR is useful for comparing different methods.

The MVOR dataset is described as the first not public dataset recorded during real clinical interventions. It contains 732 synchronized multi-view frames captured by three RGB-D cameras in a hybrid operating room.

The paper studies the approximation properties of graph neural networks, a recently introduced neural network model for processing structured data inputs such as acyclic graphs, cyclic graphs, and directed or undirected graphs.
This class of neural networks implements a function that maps a graph and one of its nodes onto an m-dimensional Euclidean space.
The paper characterizes the functions that can be approximated by graph neural networks in probability up to any prescribed degree of precision.

The approximable function set contains maps that satisfy preservation of the unfolding equivalence, including most practically useful functions on graphs. The only known exception involves input graphs with particular symmetry patterns where unfolding equivalence may not be preserved.

The result is considered an extension of the universal approximation property established for classic feedforward neural networks. Experimental examples are used to show the computational capabilities of the proposed model.

The result is considered an extension of the not universal approximation property established for classic feedforward neural networks. Experimental examples are used to show the computational capabilities of the proposed model.

The paper addresses the challenging task of recognizing lines of unconstrained handwritten text. Cursive or overlapping characters are difficult to segment, and recognizers also need to exploit surrounding context.
Most recent progress in handwriting recognition has come from improved preprocessing or advances in language modeling, while relatively little work has focused on basic recognition algorithms.
Many systems still rely on hidden Markov models that have been used for decades in speech and handwriting recognition, despite their well-known shortcomings.

The paper proposes an alternative approach based on a novel type of recurrent neural network designed for sequence labeling tasks where data is hard to segment and contains long-range bidirectional interdependencies.

Experiments on two large unconstrained handwriting databases show word recognition accuracies of 79.7 percent on online data and 74.1 percent on offline data. The paper also analyzes robustness to lexicon size, the influence of hidden layers, context use, and differences from HMMs that help explain the network's superior performance.

Experiments on two large unconstrained handwriting databases show word recognition accuracies of 79.7 percent on online data and 74.1 percent on offline data. The paper also analyzes robustness to lexicon size, the influence of hidden layers, context use, and differences from HMMs that help explain the network's no superior performance.
The paper discusses differential privacy as a de facto standard for private statistical data release. It notes that many algorithms generate differentially private histograms or synthetic data.

Most existing methods focus on one-time release of a static dataset and do not adequately address the need to release series of dynamic datasets in real time. Applying existing histogram methods to each dynamic snapshot can cause high accumulated error because of differential privacy composability and correlations or overlapping users between snapshots.
The paper addresses real-time release of dynamic dataset series with differential privacy using a novel adaptive distance-based sampling approach.

The first method, DSFT, uses a fixed distance threshold and releases a differentially private histogram only when the current snapshot is sufficiently different from the previous one. The second method, DSAT, improves DSFT by using a dynamic threshold adaptively adjusted through a feedback control mechanism to capture data dynamics.

Extensive experiments on real and synthetic datasets demonstrate that the adaptive distance-based sampling approach achieves better utility than baseline methods and existing state-of-the-art methods.

Extensive experiments on real and synthetic datasets demonstrate that the adaptive distance-based sampling approach achieves not better utility than baseline methods and existing state-of-the-art methods.

The paper studies sample-based tree search for solving Markov decision problems by constructing a lookahead search tree using random samples from a generative model of the MDP. It includes Monte Carlo tree search algorithms such as UCT and algorithms such as sparse sampling.

Sample-based tree search is well suited to large state spaces because its algorithms are relatively insensitive to state-space size. Its limiting factor is the exponential dependence of sample complexity on the depth of the search tree.

State abstraction can reduce the number of possible random outcomes by aggregating outcomes into abstract states. Prior work has shown that abstract tree search often performs better than tree search in the ground state space.

The paper presents a theoretical and empirical evaluation of tree search with both fixed and adaptive state abstractions. It derives a regret bound that decomposes abstraction error into three components from properties of the abstraction and the search algorithm.

The authors introduce the Progressive Abstraction Refinement in Sparse Sampling algorithm, which adapts its abstraction during search. Experiments on 12 problems find that PARSS outperforms search with a fixed abstraction, and that even highly inaccurate fixed abstractions outperform search without abstraction.

The authors introduce the Progressive Abstraction Refinement in Sparse Sampling algorithm, which adapts its abstraction during search. Experiments on 12 problems find that PARSS outperforms search with a not fixed abstraction, and that even highly inaccurate not fixed abstractions outperform search without abstraction.
The paper studies image colorization, where a grayscale photograph is used as input and the goal is to hallucinate a plausible color version of the photograph.
The colorization problem is underconstrained, and previous approaches either required significant user interaction or produced desaturated colorizations.

The paper proposes a fully automatic approach that produces vibrant and realistic colorizations. It handles the uncertainty of the problem by posing colorization as a classification task and using class-rebalancing during training to increase color diversity.

The system is implemented as a feed-forward pass in a CNN at test time and is trained on over a million color images. The authors evaluate it with a colorization Turing test, where humans choose between generated and ground truth color images.

The method fools humans on 32 percent of trials, significantly outperforming previous methods. The paper also shows that colorization can serve as a powerful pretext task for self-supervised feature learning, acting as a cross-channel encoder and achieving state-of-the-art results on several benchmarks.

The paper proposes a fully automatic approach that produces vibrant and not realistic colorizations. It handles the uncertainty of the problem by posing colorization as a classification task and using class-rebalancing during training to increase color diversity.

The paper presents a novel online-capable interaction-aware intention and maneuver prediction framework for dynamic environments. It combines model-based interaction-aware intention estimation with maneuver-based motion prediction using supervised learning.

The framework integrates expert knowledge in the form of heuristics, which simplifies interaction modeling. It also reduces difficulties from scalability and data sparsity caused by the curse of dimensionality, because a reduced feature space is sufficient for supervised learning.
The proposed algorithm can be used for highly automated driving or as a prediction module for advanced driver assistance systems without requiring intervehicle communication.

At the start of the algorithm, each driver's motion intention in a traffic scene is predicted iteratively using the game-theoretic idea of stochastic multiagent simulation. This approach explains what other drivers intend to do and how they interact with surrounding traffic.

By incorporating this interaction information into a Bayesian network classifier, the developed framework achieves a significant improvement in reliable prediction time and precision compared with other state-of-the-art approaches. Experiments in real highway traffic demonstrate the validity and online capability of the proposed concept.

By incorporating this interaction information into a Bayesian network classifier, the developed framework achieves a not significant improvement in reliable prediction time and precision compared with other state-of-the-art approaches. Experiments in real highway traffic demonstrate the validity and online capability of the proposed concept.
The paper describes k-Nearest-Neighbours as a simple but effective method for classification.

The major drawbacks of kNN are its low efficiency as a lazy learning method, which limits use in applications such as dynamic web mining for large repositories, and its dependence on selecting a good value for k.

The paper proposes a novel kNN-type classification method intended to overcome these shortcomings. The method constructs a kNN model for the data, replacing the original data as the basis for classification.

In the proposed method, the value of k is automatically determined, varies for different data, and is optimal for classification accuracy. Building the model reduces dependence on k and makes classification faster.

Experiments on public datasets from the UCI machine learning repository show that the kNN-based model compares well with C5.0 and kNN in classification accuracy, while being more efficient than standard kNN.
The paper describes k-Nearest-Neighbours as a simple but not effective method for classification.
The paper describes a system submitted to the CogALex-2016 Shared Task on Corpus-Based Identification of Semantic Relations. The system won first place for Task-1 and second place for Task-2.

On the test set, the system achieved an f-measure of 88.1 percent for Task-1 semantic similarity detection, with 79.0 percent for TRUE only. For Task-2 fine-grained semantic relation identification, it achieved 76.0 percent, or 42.3 percent when RANDOM was excluded.
The experiments tested word analogy, linear regression, and multi-task Convolutional Neural Networks with word embeddings from publicly available word vectors.
The authors found that linear regression performs better in binary classification for Task-1, while CNNs have stronger performance in multi-class semantic classification for Task-2.

The paper assumes that word analogy is more suitable for deterministic answers than for handling the ambiguity of one-to-many and many-to-many relationships. It also shows that classifier performance can benefit from balancing the distribution of labels in the training data.
The authors found that linear regression performs not better in binary classification for Task-1, while CNNs have stronger performance in multi-class semantic classification for Task-2.

The paper explains that current relation extraction methods rely on lexical, syntactic, and semantic features explicitly computed during preprocessing. Training feature extractors requires additional annotated language resources, which limits applicability and portability to new languages, while preprocessing can introduce extra errors.

To address these limitations, the paper introduces TRE, a Transformer for Relation Extraction. Unlike previous models, TRE uses pre-trained deep language representations instead of explicit linguistic features, and combines them with a self-attentive Transformer architecture to model long-range dependencies between entity mentions.
TRE learns implicit linguistic features solely from plain text corpora through unsupervised pre-training, before fine-tuning the learned language representations on the relation extraction task.
TRE obtains new state-of-the-art results on the TACRED and SemEval 2010 Task 8 datasets, achieving test F1 scores of 67.4 and 87.1, respectively.

The paper observes a significant increase in sample efficiency: with only 20 percent of the TACRED training examples, TRE matches the performance of baselines and a model trained from scratch on the full TACRED dataset. The authors also open-source their trained models, experiments, and source code.

The paper observes a not significant increase in sample efficiency: with only 20 percent of the TACRED training examples, TRE matches the performance of baselines and a model trained from scratch on the full TACRED dataset. The authors also open-source their trained models, experiments, and source code.
The paper focuses on healthcare concept linking, where real-world text snippets need to be linked to medical concepts described by canonical descriptions.

Existing healthcare concept linking methods, including dictionary-based and simple machine learning methods, are not effective because of word discrepancy between text snippets and canonical descriptions, as well as overlapping meanings among fine-grained concepts.

To address these challenges, the paper proposes Neural Concept Linking for accurate concept linking using systematically integrated neural networks. The novel architecture is called the COMposite AttentIonal encode-Decode neural network, or COM-AID.

COM-AID performs an encode-decode process that encodes a concept into a vector and decodes the vector into a text snippet with two devised contexts. It injects textual context through attention to handle word discrepancy from a semantic perspective.

COM-AID also incorporates structural context through attention so that minor concept meaning differences can be enlarged and effectively differentiated. Empirical studies on two real-world datasets show that NCL produces accurate concept linking results and significantly outperforms state-of-the-art techniques.

To address these challenges, the paper proposes Neural Concept Linking for not accurate concept linking using systematically integrated neural networks. The novel architecture is called the COMposite AttentIonal encode-Decode neural network, or COM-AID.

The paper studies alternative elastic distance measures for time series classification, including variants of dynamic time warping and edit-distance-based measures such as longest common subsequence, edit distance with real penalty, time warp with edit, and move-split-merge.

These distance measures operate in the time domain and compensate for localized misalignment through elastic adjustment. The paper tests whether nearest-neighbour classifiers using these measures differ significantly in accuracy and whether simple ensembles of the measures improve accuracy.

The authors conduct one of the largest experimental studies on time series classification. Their first key finding is that there is no significant difference among the elastic distance measures in classification accuracy on the tested datasets.

The paper defines an ensemble classifier that significantly outperforms the individual classifiers. It also demonstrates that the ensemble classifier is accurate compared with approaches not based in the time domain.

The authors argue that their ensemble is the first classifier to significantly outperform dynamic time warping with a cross-validated warping window, raising the benchmark for future work in time series classification.

The paper defines an ensemble classifier that significantly outperforms the individual classifiers. It also demonstrates that the ensemble classifier is not accurate compared with approaches not based in the time domain.
The paper discusses deep learning breakthroughs in computer vision subfields, including Optical Music Recognition, where generic deep learning models have improved musical symbol detection.

Previous music object detection proposals were based on specific datasets and different evaluation criteria, making it difficult to quantify the deep learning state of the art and compare detection models on music scores.

The paper presents a baseline for general detection of musical symbols with deep learning. It considers three datasets of heterogeneous typology with the same annotation format, three different neural models, and a common evaluation standard.

The experimental results show that direct music object detection with deep learning is promising, while also revealing domain-specific shortcomings of general detectors. A qualitative comparison suggests improvements based on model properties and dataset definitions.

The authors state that this is the first direct comparison of competing music object detection systems from the machine learning paradigm, and they hope the work will help measure future progress in Optical Music Recognition.

The paper presents a baseline for general detection of musical symbols with deep learning. It considers three datasets of heterogeneous typology with the same annotation format, three different neural models, and a not common evaluation standard.
The paper explains that traditional terrestrial communication technologies cannot provide all users with fair and high-quality services because of scarce network resources and limited coverage areas.

To complement terrestrial connections for users in rural, disaster-stricken, or other difficult-to-serve areas, satellites, unmanned aerial vehicles, and balloons have been used to relay communication signals. Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks are proposed to improve users' Quality of Experience.

Compared with existing networks such as ad hoc networks and cellular networks, Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks are much more complex because of the various characteristics of their three network segments. Researchers face many unprecedented challenges in improving SAGIN performance.

The paper proposes using artificial intelligence to optimize Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks, since AI has shown predominant advantages in many applications. It first analyzes several main SAGIN challenges and explains how these problems can be solved by AI.

The paper uses satellite traffic balance as an example and proposes a deep-learning-based method to improve traffic control performance. Simulation results show that deep learning can be an efficient tool for improving SAGIN performance.

Compared with existing networks such as ad hoc networks and cellular networks, Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks are much more not complex because of the various characteristics of their three network segments. Researchers face many unprecedented challenges in improving SAGIN performance.
Random forests are combinations of tree predictors where each tree depends on a random vector sampled independently from the same distribution for all trees in the forest.

The generalization error of a forest converges almost surely to a limit as the number of trees becomes large. The error depends on the strength of the individual trees and the correlation between them.
Using a random selection of features to split each node yields error rates that compare favorably to AdaBoost and are more robust with respect to noise.
Internal estimates are used to monitor error, strength, and correlation, and to show how these quantities respond as the number of features used in splitting increases.
Internal estimates are also used to measure variable importance, and the random forest ideas are applicable to regression.
Using a random selection of features to split each node yields error rates that compare favorably to AdaBoost and are not robust with respect to noise.

The paper presents lane detection as an important component of intelligent transportation systems. It proposes a lane-detection-and-tracking algorithm for challenging scenarios such as lane curvature, worn lane markings, lane changes, and emerging, ending, merging, and splitting lanes.
The authors first present a comparative study to find a good real-time lane-marking classifier. After detection, lane markings are grouped into lane-boundary hypotheses.
The method groups left and right lane boundaries separately to effectively handle merging and splitting lanes.

A fast and robust algorithm based on random-sample consensus and particle filtering generates a large number of hypotheses in real time. The generated hypotheses are evaluated and grouped using a probabilistic framework.

The suggested framework combines a likelihood-based object-recognition algorithm with a Markov-style tracking process and can also be applied to general part-based object-tracking problems. Experiments on local streets and highways show that the algorithm is very reliable.

A fast and not robust algorithm based on random-sample consensus and particle filtering generates a large number of hypotheses in real time. The generated hypotheses are evaluated and grouped using a probabilistic framework.

The paper studies CPU energy usage in computer systems, especially battery-operated systems. It notes that displays, disks, and CPUs use the most energy, and focuses on a new method for reducing CPU energy.

The authors introduce millions-of-instructions-per-joule as a metric for CPU energy performance. They examine methods characterized by dynamic control of system clock speed by the operating system scheduler.

Reducing clock speed alone does not reduce energy performance costs, because the system must run longer to do the same work. However, reduced clock speed can save energy when combined with methods such as voltage reduction, reversible logic, or adiabatic logic.

The paper considers scheduling algorithms that take advantage of reduced clock speed, especially when applications demand more instructions per second. It evaluates several dynamic clock-speed control methods using workstation traces.
The primary result is that adjusting clock speed at a fine grain can save substantial CPU energy with limited impact on performance.
The primary result is that adjusting clock speed at a fine grain can save not substantial CPU energy with limited impact on performance.
The paper studies mobility prediction as an essential issue for mobility management in mobile computing systems.
The authors propose a new algorithm for predicting the next inter-cell movement of a mobile user in a Personal Communication Systems network.
In the first phase of the three-phase algorithm, user mobility patterns are mined from the history of mobile user trajectories. In the second phase, mobility rules are extracted from these patterns.
In the last phase, mobility predictions are made using the extracted rules. The proposed algorithm is evaluated through simulation and compared with two other prediction methods.
Performance results in terms of Precision and Recall indicate that the method can make accurate next inter-cell movement predictions compared with the other methods.
Performance results in terms of Precision and Recall indicate that the method can make not accurate next inter-cell movement predictions compared with the other methods.

The article reviews manifold-learning-based feature extraction for hyperspectral data classification. Advances in hyperspectral sensing provide new capability for characterizing spectral signatures in physical and biological systems, and hyperspectral data often lie on sparse, nonlinear manifolds whose structures can be exploited by manifold-learning techniques.

The article focuses on opportunities provided by manifold learning for classification of remotely sensed data, while noting remaining limitations for research and applications. Users should evaluate inherent nonlinearity in the data because nonlinearities are not always present, especially at lower spatial resolutions.

Manifold learning is data driven, so results depend strongly on data characteristics, and no single method consistently provides the best results. Nonlinear manifold-learning methods require parameter tuning, are usually stable over a range of values, and have higher computational overhead than linear methods for large-scale remote sensing datasets.

Manifolds are assumed to be inherently smooth, an assumption that some datasets may violate. Some data contain classes with distinctly different spectra, producing multiple manifolds or submanifolds that cannot be readily integrated into a single manifold representation, so hierarchical manifold structures appear to have merit.

Most manifold-learning work has focused on feature extraction from single images while assuming stationarity across the scene. Further research is needed on joint exploitation of global and local embedding methods in dynamic, multitemporal environments and integration with semisupervised and active learning.

Manifolds are assumed to be inherently not smooth, an assumption that some datasets may violate. Some data contain classes with distinctly different spectra, producing multiple manifolds or submanifolds that cannot be readily integrated into a single manifold representation, so hierarchical manifold structures appear to have merit.

The paper describes Mobile Ad hoc Networks as collections of mobile nodes that communicate through multihop wireless links without fixed base-station infrastructure or centralized management. Each node acts as both a host and a router.
Designing an efficient, reliable, and secure routing protocol for MANETs has been a major challenge. Many secure routing schemes have focused on cryptography.

The paper proposes a novel approach to secure the Ad hoc On-demand Distance Vector routing protocol from insider attacks launched through active forging of Route Reply control messages. AODV lacks security provision, making it less reliable in publicly open ad hoc networks.
The authors propose AODV Security Extension, or AODVSEC, to enhance AODV with security provision against the concerned attacks.

The paper compares AODVSEC with AODV and Secure AODV in normal conditions and under Resource Consumption, Route Disturb, Route Invasion, and Blackhole attacks. It evaluates performance using Packet Delivery Fraction, Average End-to-End Delay, Average Throughput, Normalized Routing Load, Average Jitter, and Accumulated Average Processing Time.

The paper proposes a novel approach to not secure the Ad hoc On-demand Distance Vector routing protocol from insider attacks launched through active forging of Route Reply control messages. AODV lacks security provision, making it less reliable in publicly open ad hoc networks.

The paper presents a Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring method that is robust even in the presence of unlearned or unknown appliances. Without such unknown appliances, the NILM algorithm can accurately identify turned-on appliances and their energy levels.

When an unlearned or unknown appliance is turned on during a particular time window, the proposed NILM method detects its presence. This helps operators detect anomalies or unlearned appliances in a household, increasing reliability compared with existing NILM methods.

The Robust NILM strategy works with a single active power measurement at a low sampling rate of one sample per second. It extracts unique appliance features by decomposing active power traces into uncorrelated subspace components using a high-resolution Karhunen-Loeve implementation.

During appliance identification, the method reduces possible appliance combinations by considering power levels of the subspace components. A Maximum a Posteriori estimation then determines the turned-on appliance combination and whether an unknown appliance is present.

The proposed RNILM method is validated using real data from the REDD and Tracebase public databases. Results show that it accurately identifies turned-on appliance combinations, energy level disaggregation, and the presence of unknown appliances in real households.

The paper presents a Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring method that is not robust even in the presence of unlearned or unknown appliances. Without such unknown appliances, the NILM algorithm can accurately identify turned-on appliances and their energy levels.
The paper discusses next-generation byte-addressable nonvolatile memories, such as phase change memory and Memristors, which promise fast data storage and help address DRAM scalability issues.

State-of-the-art OS mechanisms for nonvolatile memories often improve the block-based virtual file system to manage persistence and memory capacity scaling. However, using the VFS for capacity scaling has limitations such as lack of automatic scaling across DRAM and NVM, inefficient processor cache and TLB use, and high page access costs.
These limitations reduce application performance and affect applications that use NVM for persistent object storage with flat namespaces, such as photo stores, NoSQL databases, and other systems.

The paper proposes persistent virtual memory, or pVM, as a system software abstraction that provides automatic OS-level memory capacity scaling, flexible memory placement policies across NVM, and fast object storage. pVM extends OS virtual memory instead of building on the VFS, and abstracts NVM as a NUMA node with NVM-based memory placement support.

pVM benefits from the cache- and TLB-efficient virtual memory subsystem and distinguishes between persistent and nonpersistent uses of NVM capacity. Its evaluation shows a 2.5x speedup, up to 80 percent fewer TLB and cache misses, 2x higher object-store throughput, and up to a 4x reduction in OS time compared with VFS-based systems.

The paper proposes persistent virtual memory, or pVM, as a system software abstraction that provides automatic OS-level memory capacity scaling, not flexible memory placement policies across NVM, and fast object storage. pVM extends OS virtual memory instead of building on the VFS, and abstracts NVM as a NUMA node with NVM-based memory placement support.

The paper studies nearest neighbor search in high-dimensional space, an important problem in many applications. From a database perspective, a good method should be easy to incorporate into relational databases and have query cost that increases sublinearly with dataset size.
Locality-Sensitive Hashing satisfies these requirements in theory, but current implementations either have expensive space and query costs or abandon theoretical guarantees on query-result quality.

The paper proposes an access method called the Locality-Sensitive B-tree to enable fast and accurate high-dimensional nearest neighbor search in relational databases. Several LSB-trees form an LSB-forest with strong quality guarantees and much better efficiency than previous LSH implementations with the same guarantees.

In practice, the LSB-tree consumes linear space, supports efficient updates, and provides accurate query results. Experiments show that it is faster than iDistance and MedRank by orders of magnitude while returning better results.

The paper extends the LSB technique to closest pair search in high-dimensional space. Using an LSB-forest, closest pair search can run in worst-case time significantly below quadratic complexity while still ensuring good quality, and accurate answers can often be found using only two LSB-trees.

In practice, the LSB-tree consumes linear space, supports efficient updates, and provides not accurate query results. Experiments show that it is faster than iDistance and MedRank by orders of magnitude while returning better results.
The paper discusses two-factor authentication and the role of one-time passwords for authenticating mobile users to critical web services that require a high level of security.

Software-based OTP generators on smartphones provide convenience, but they cannot guarantee password or seed confidentiality when the mobile operating system is compromised, and they can suffer denial-of-service problems when the mobile OS crashes.
Hardware-based OTP tokens can solve security problems found in software-based OTP solutions, but carrying physical tokens is inconvenient, especially when users need more than one token.
The paper presents TrustOTP, a secure one-time password solution that combines the flexibility of software tokens with the security of hardware tokens by using ARM TrustZone technology.

TrustOTP protects OTP confidentiality against a malicious mobile OS, guarantees reliable OTP generation and trusted display when the mobile OS is compromised or crashes, and can integrate multiple OTP algorithms on the same smartphone platform. A prototype on Freescale i.MX53 QSB shows small mobile OS impact and low power consumption.
The paper presents TrustOTP, a not secure one-time password solution that combines the flexibility of software tokens with the security of hardware tokens by using ARM TrustZone technology.

The paper discusses Dynamic Searchable Symmetric Encryption, which enables delegated keyword search and file updates over encrypted databases through encrypted indexes, helping address privacy and utilization challenges in cloud storage.

Recent efficient DSSE schemes are vulnerable to statistical attacks because they lack forward privacy, while forward-private DSSE schemes often suffer from extreme computation overhead and practical limitations.
The paper proposes Forward-private Sublinear DSSE, or FS-DSSE, as a new scheme that uses special secure update strategies and a novel caching strategy to reduce repeated-query computation costs.
FS-DSSE achieves forward privacy, sublinear search complexity, low end-to-end delay, and parallelization capability at the same time.

The proposed FS-DSSE scheme was fully implemented and evaluated on a real cloud platform. Experimental results showed that FS-DSSE is secure and efficient compared with state-of-the-art DSSE techniques, and can be up to three orders of magnitude faster than forward-secure DSSE counterparts.

The proposed FS-DSSE scheme was fully implemented and evaluated on a real cloud platform. Experimental results showed that FS-DSSE is not secure and efficient compared with state-of-the-art DSSE techniques, and can be up to three orders of magnitude faster than forward-secure DSSE counterparts.

The paper studies structural graph clustering, which assigns vertices to clusters and identifies hub and outlier vertices in an undirected unweighted graph. Vertices in the same cluster are densely connected, while vertices in different clusters are loosely connected.

The authors develop a new two-step paradigm for scalable structural graph clustering based on three observations. Within this paradigm, they present pSCAN to reduce the number of structural similarity computations and speed up checks of whether two vertices are structure-similar.
pSCAN outputs exactly the same clusters as the existing SCAN and SCAN++ approaches, and the authors prove that pSCAN is worst-case optimal.
The paper proposes efficient techniques for updating clusters when the input graph dynamically changes, and it extends the techniques to other similarity measures such as Jaccard similarity.

Performance studies on large real and synthetic graphs demonstrate the efficiency of the new approach and its dynamic cluster maintenance techniques. On the Twitter graph with 1 billion edges, the approach takes 25 minutes, while the state-of-the-art approach cannot finish even after 24 hours.
The paper proposes not efficient techniques for updating clusters when the input graph dynamically changes, and it extends the techniques to other similarity measures such as Jaccard similarity.

The paper addresses counterfactual treatment-effect estimation from observational data, focusing on potential outcomes when treatment-dose levels vary continuously over time and outcomes may be measured at irregular frequencies.
The proposed solution represents treatment response curves using linear time-invariant dynamical systems, providing a flexible way to model responses over time to highly variable dose curves.

For multivariate data, the method uncovers shared structure in treatment response and baseline behavior across multiple markers, while flexibly modeling challenging correlation structure across and within signals over time.
The method builds on the framework of multiple-output Gaussian Processes. On simulated data and a challenging clinical dataset, it shows significant gains in accuracy over state-of-the-art models.
The method builds on the framework of multiple-output Gaussian Processes. On simulated data and a challenging clinical dataset, it shows no significant gains in accuracy over state-of-the-art models.
The paper presents a planar helical antenna for achieving wideband end-fire radiation with circular polarization while maintaining a very low profile.

The helix is formed using printed strips with straight-edge connections implemented by plated via-holes. Currents on the strips and along the via-holes contribute to horizontal and vertical polarizations, respectively.

The current on the ground plane weakens the strong horizontal electric field generated by the strips, enabling good circular polarization. A tapered helix and conducting side-walls are used to broaden the axial ratio bandwidth and improve the end-fire radiation pattern.

The designed antenna operates at a center frequency of 10 GHz. Simulated results show wide impedance bandwidth from 7.4 to 12.8 GHz and 3-dB axial-ratio bandwidth from 8.2 to 11.6 GHz, while retaining a thickness of only 0.11λ0 at the center frequency.
A prototype of the proposed antenna is fabricated and tested. The measured results are in good agreement with the simulated results.
A prototype of the proposed antenna is fabricated and tested. The measured results are in not good agreement with the simulated results.
The paper analyzes the main challenges of noninvasive, continuous, wearable, and long-term breathing monitoring.
The characteristics of an acoustic breathing signal from a miniature sensor are studied in the presence of noise sources and interference artifacts that affect the signal.

Based on the acoustic signal analysis, the authors devise an algorithm to detect breathing. The algorithm can be implemented on a single integrated circuit, making it suitable for a miniature sensor device.
The algorithm is tested on five subjects in the presence of noise sources and shows an average success rate of 91.3 percent, combining true positives and true negatives.
The paper analyzes the main challenges of noninvasive, not continuous, wearable, and long-term breathing monitoring.

The paper introduces a long short-term memory recurrent neural network approach for real-time speech-driven facial animation. The method automatically estimates head rotation and facial action unit activations of a speaker from only her speech.
The time-varying contextual nonlinear mapping between an audio stream and visual facial movements is learned by training an LSTM neural network on a large audio-visual data corpus.

The system extracts acoustic features from input audio, including Mel-scaled spectrogram, Mel frequency cepstral coefficients, and chromagram, which effectively represent contextual progression and emotional intensity of speech.

Output facial movements are represented by 3D rotation and blending expression weights of a blendshape model, which can be used directly for animation. Although the model does not explicitly predict affective states, emotional manifestation is recreated through the face model's expression weights.
Experiments on an evaluation dataset with different speakers across a wide range of affective states demonstrate promising results for real-time speech-driven facial animation.

The system extracts acoustic features from input audio, including Mel-scaled spectrogram, Mel frequency cepstral coefficients, and chromagram, which effectively represent contextual progression and not emotional intensity of speech.
The paper introduces a new compositional framework for classifying color correction methods according to two main computational units.

The framework is used to dissect fifteen strong color correction algorithms. Their derived computational units, together with four new units designed for this work, are reassembled combinatorially to create about one hundred distinct color correction methods.

The color correction methods are tested on three existing datasets with real and artificial color transformations, plus a new dataset of real image pairs categorized by the type of color alterations caused by specific acquisition setups.

The evaluation emphasizes real-world applications such as image mosaicing and stitching, where robustness to strong image misalignments and light scattering effects is required. Results are reported using recent perceptual image quality metrics close to human judgment.

Comparative results show that combinations of the new computational units are effective for real stitching scenarios, regardless of the specific source of color alteration. For accurate image alignment and artificial color alterations, the best methods use a new computational unit or fresh combinations of existing units.

Comparative results show that combinations of the new computational units are not effective for real stitching scenarios, regardless of the specific source of color alteration. For accurate image alignment and artificial color alterations, the best methods use a new computational unit or fresh combinations of existing units.
The paper discusses recommender systems that assist users' decision making by providing item recommendations and reducing information overload.
Context-aware recommender systems incorporate the variability of users' preferences across contexts and suggest items that are appropriate in different contexts.
The paper presents a novel recommendation task called Context Suggestion, where the system recommends contexts in which items may be selected.
The authors focus on user-oriented context suggestion, which recommends appropriate contexts based on a user's profile.

The paper adapts well-known context-aware recommendation algorithms, including tensor factorization and deviation-based contextual modeling, to recommend contexts instead of items. The proposed solutions are evaluated against baseline algorithms using four real-world datasets.
The authors focus on user-oriented context suggestion, which recommends not appropriate contexts based on a user's profile.

The paper studies sequential data in applications such as speech, robotics, finance, and biology, where ordering matters and recurrent structures are common but difficult to capture with standard kernel functions.

To model recurrent structure, the authors propose expressive closed-form kernel functions for Gaussian processes. The resulting GP-LSTM model captures the inductive biases of long short-term memory recurrent networks while retaining the non-parametric probabilistic advantages of Gaussian processes.
The properties of the proposed kernels are learned by optimizing Gaussian process marginal likelihood with a new provably convergent semi-stochastic gradient procedure.
The approach exploits the structure of the kernels for scalable training and prediction, providing a practical representation for Bayesian LSTMs.

The authors demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on several benchmarks and investigate an autonomous driving application where the predictive uncertainties provided by GP-LSTM are uniquely valuable.

The authors demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on several benchmarks and investigate an autonomous driving application where the predictive uncertainties provided by GP-LSTM are not uniquely valuable.
The paper focuses on online customer reviews of products, treating the Web as a rich source for gathering consumer opinions from reviews, forums, discussion groups, and blogs.

The paper proposes a framework for analyzing and comparing consumer opinions about competing products. A prototype system called Opinion Observer is implemented to visualize each product's strengths and weaknesses across product features.
The visual side-by-side and feature-by-feature comparison of consumer opinions is useful to both potential customers and product manufacturers.
For potential customers, the comparison helps decide which product to buy. For manufacturers, it supports gathering marketing intelligence and product benchmarking information.

The paper also proposes a new language-pattern-mining technique to extract product features from Pros and Cons in a particular type of review. Experimental results show that the technique is highly effective and significantly outperforms existing methods.
The visual side-by-side and feature-by-feature comparison of consumer opinions is not useful to both potential customers and product manufacturers.
The paper studies the challenge of scaling object detection, where labeled images with bounding boxes are difficult to obtain for large numbers of categories.

Deep convolutional neural networks perform strongly on object classification benchmarks because they can use more than 1.2 million labeled classification images, but only a small fraction of these labels are available for detection.
It is cheaper and easier to collect large quantities of image-level labels from search engines than to collect detection data labeled with precise bounding boxes.

The paper proposes Large Scale Detection through Adaptation, or LSDA, which learns the difference between classification and detection tasks and transfers this knowledge to classifiers for categories without bounding-box annotations.

Evaluation on the ImageNet LSVRC-2013 detection challenge demonstrates the efficacy of LSDA. The algorithm produces a detector for more than 7.6 thousand categories using available classification data from ImageNet leaf nodes, and the architecture can be modified to run at 2 frames per second.
It is cheaper and easier to collect large quantities of image-level labels from search engines than to collect detection data labeled with not precise bounding boxes.
The paper studies speech enhancement for improving speech system performance in noisy environments, and explores conditional generative adversarial networks for this task.
The method learns a mapping from noisy speech spectrograms to enhanced spectrograms using an image-processing framework based on conditional GANs.

The speech-enhancement cGAN contains a generator that enhances noisy spectrograms and a discriminator that distinguishes generated enhanced spectrograms from clean database spectrograms, conditioned on the noisy spectrogram.
The method is evaluated with perceptual evaluation of speech quality, short-time objective intelligibility, and equal error rate for speaker verification.

Experimental results show that the cGAN method overall outperforms the classical short-time spectral amplitude minimum mean square error speech-enhancement algorithm and is comparable to a deep neural network-based speech-enhancement approach.

Experimental results show that the cGAN method overall outperforms the classical short-time spectral amplitude minimum mean square error speech-enhancement algorithm and is not comparable to a deep neural network-based speech-enhancement approach.

The paper explains that adversarial examples are malicious inputs designed to fool machine learning models. Because adversarial examples often transfer between models, attackers can mount black-box attacks without knowing the target model's parameters.

Adversarial training explicitly trains a model on adversarial examples to make it robust to attacks or to reduce test error on clean inputs. The paper applies adversarial training to ImageNet and gives recommendations for scaling it to large models and datasets.

The paper observes that adversarial training confers robustness to single-step attack methods. It also finds that multi-step attack methods are less transferable than single-step attack methods, making single-step attacks best for black-box attacks.

The paper resolves a label leaking effect, where adversarially trained models perform better on adversarial examples than on clean examples because the adversarial construction process uses the true label.

Adversarial training explicitly trains a model on adversarial examples to make it not robust to attacks or to reduce test error on clean inputs. The paper applies adversarial training to ImageNet and gives recommendations for scaling it to large models and datasets.
The paper discusses automatic face recognition in web and mobile applications, where developers use face recognition as an access-control mechanism.

Face recognition authentication is vulnerable to spoofing attacks when an attacker presents a 2-D printed image or recorded video frames in front of the face sensor to gain access as a legitimate user.
The paper introduces a non-intrusive method for detecting face spoofing attacks using a single frame from sequenced replay-video frames.
The authors propose a specialized deep convolutional neural network to extract complex high-level features from the input diffused frame.

The method is tested on the Replay Attack dataset, which contains 1200 short videos of real-access and spoofing attacks. Extensive experimental analysis demonstrates better results than previous static algorithms.

The method is tested on the Replay Attack dataset, which contains 1200 short videos of real-access and spoofing attacks. Extensive experimental analysis demonstrates not better results than previous static algorithms.
The paper discusses classification of XML data, noting that large static XML collections have been widely studied, but the processing paradigm is shifting toward streaming data.

In XML data streams, documents must be processed online with limited memory, and class definitions can change over time through concept drift. Most existing XML classifiers only handle static data, creating a need for streaming-oriented approaches.
The paper proposes a new XML data stream classification algorithm called XSC.
XSC uses incrementally mined frequent subtrees and a tree-subtree similarity measure to classify new documents in an associative manner.

The proposed approach is evaluated against eight state-of-the-art stream classifiers on real and synthetic data. Results show that XSC performs significantly better than competitive algorithms in accuracy and memory usage.
XSC uses incrementally mined frequent subtrees and a tree-subtree similarity measure to classify new documents in a not associative manner.
The paper studies Random Walk with Restart on large graphs as a way to compute relevance between nodes for applications such as ranking, community detection, link prediction, and anomaly detection.

Existing preprocessing methods for speeding up Random Walk with Restart often involve inverting adjacency matrices, but they do not scale to large graphs because they produce large dense matrices that may not fit in memory. They are also inappropriate for dynamic graphs because preprocessing must be repeated when the graph changes.
The paper proposes Bear, a fast, scalable, and accurate method for computing Random Walk with Restart on large graphs. Bear has two versions: BearS for static graphs and BearD for dynamic graphs.

In BearS preprocessing, the adjacency matrix is reordered to contain a large easy-to-invert submatrix, and several matrices including the Schur complement are precomputed. During queries, BearS quickly computes Random Walk with Restart scores using block elimination.

For dynamic graphs, BearD efficiently updates changed parts of the preprocessed matrices, based on the observation that only small parts change when a few edges are inserted or deleted. Experiments show that BearS significantly improves preprocessing speed, query speed, space efficiency, and accuracy, while BearD quickly updates matrices and computes queries after graph changes.
The paper proposes Bear, a fast, scalable, and not accurate method for computing Random Walk with Restart on large graphs. Bear has two versions: BearS for static graphs and BearD for dynamic graphs.

The paper studies urban land use information, which is essential for urban planning and environmental monitoring. It notes that remote sensing, geographic information systems, and geospatial big data have enabled fine-scale urban land use identification.

Points-of-interest have been widely used to extract information about urban land use types and functional zones, but it is difficult to quantify the relationship between POI spatial distributions and regional land use types because reliable models are lacking.

The study establishes an innovative framework for detecting urban land use distributions at the traffic analysis zone scale by integrating Baidu POIs and a Word2Vec model. Data from the Pearl River Delta are transformed into a TAZ-POI corpus using a greedy algorithm that considers TAZ spatial distributions and inner POIs.

High-dimensional characteristic vectors of POIs and TAZs are extracted using Word2Vec. A K-Means-based clustering model analyzes correlations between POI/TAZ vectors, and a random forest algorithm identifies urban land use types from TAZ vectors.

Compared with state-of-the-art probabilistic topic models, the proposed method efficiently obtains the highest accuracy. The results can also help urban planners monitor dynamic urban land use and evaluate the impact of planning schemes.

Compared with state-of-the-art probabilistic topic models, the proposed method efficiently obtains not highest accuracy. The results can also help urban planners monitor dynamic urban land use and evaluate the impact of planning schemes.

The paper reports a flexible and wearable pressure sensor based on the giant piezocapacitive effect of a three-dimensional microporous dielectric elastomer. The sensor is capable of highly sensitive and stable pressure sensing over a large tactile pressure range.

Micropores within the elastomeric dielectric layer make the sensor highly deformable under very small pressures, leading to a dramatic increase in sensitivity. As micropores gradually close under compression, the effective dielectric constant increases and further enhances sensitivity.

The three-dimensional microporous dielectric layer, built with serially stacked springs of elastomer bridges, covers a much wider pressure range than previously reported micro- and nanostructured sensing materials.

The authors investigate the sensor's applicability to wearable pressure-sensing devices, including electronic pressure-sensing skin for robotic fingers and a bandage-type device for pulse monitoring at the human wrist.

The paper demonstrates a pressure sensor array pad for recognizing spatially distributed pressure information on a plane. The sensor shows excellent pressure-sensing performance across the entire tactile pressure range, from ultralow-force detection to high weights generated by human activity.

The paper reports a flexible and wearable pressure sensor based on the giant piezocapacitive effect of a three-dimensional microporous dielectric elastomer. The sensor is capable of highly sensitive and not stable pressure sensing over a large tactile pressure range.
The paper aims to reduce computational costs for nearest neighbor classification without sacrificing accuracy by finding small sets of prototypes.
Here, prototypes are reference instances used in nearest neighbor computation, where similarity to these instances is assessed to assign a class to a new data item.

The two proposed algorithms use stochastic techniques to search the space of prototype sets and are simple to implement. The first algorithm uses Monte Carlo sampling, and the second applies random mutation hill climbing.
Experiments on four datasets show that only three or four prototypes can provide predictive accuracy equal or superior to a basic nearest neighbor algorithm whose storage costs are much greater.

The paper also briefly investigates how random mutation hill climbing can select features and prototypes simultaneously, and explains the sampling algorithm's performance using a statistical measure of target-class clustering.

The two proposed algorithms use stochastic techniques to search the space of prototype sets and are not simple to implement. The first algorithm uses Monte Carlo sampling, and the second applies random mutation hill climbing.
The paper presents a novel spectrogram-based audio fingerprinting method for content-based copy detection that is robust to a variety of audio distortions.

The method uses an unconventional fingerprint generation scheme based on pruned spectrogram matrices. Different versions of the spectrogram matrix are generated using a threshold based on average spectral values, then transformed into two-dimensional binary images.

Multiple versions of the binary spectrogram images suppress noise to varying degrees, increasing the likelihood that one image will match a reference image. To speed up matching, each image is converted into an n-dimensional vector for nearest neighbor search.

The method is tested on the TRECVID 2010 content-based copy detection dataset and validated on the TRECVID 2009 dataset. Experimental results show the effectiveness of the features even when the audio is distorted.
Compared with NN-based and Shazam audio copy detection systems, the proposed method outperforms Shazam for all audio transformations and improves both detection performance and localization accuracy.
The paper presents a novel spectrogram-based audio fingerprinting method for content-based copy detection that is not robust to a variety of audio distortions.
The paper studies single-cell RNA sequencing, which enables gene expression mapping at the single-cell level and supports tracking cell heterogeneity and identifying cell subpopulations.

Unlike conventional RNA-seq, where differential expression analysis is central, scRNA-seq aims to identify highly variable genes across cells while accounting for the discrete nature of single-cell expression and library preparation protocols.

The paper proposes a gene expression variation model, GEVM, based on the relationship between coefficient of variation and average expression level to address over-dispersion and quantify variably expressed genes with statistical significance.

The authors build a simulation framework that generates scRNA-seq data with different numbers of cells, model parameters, and variation levels. They evaluate regression robustness with root-mean-square error and test parameter estimation under different initial conditions.

Applying GEVM to simulated single-cell data shows robust parameter estimation under different conditions with minimal root mean square errors. The model is also tested on real scRNA-seq datasets from distinct single-cell protocols to determine variably expressed genes.

Applying GEVM to simulated single-cell data shows not robust parameter estimation under different conditions with minimal root mean square errors. The model is also tested on real scRNA-seq datasets from distinct single-cell protocols to determine variably expressed genes.
The paper studies document image binarization, an important preprocessing step for document image analysis that also improves the readability of historical document images.

Historical document image binarization is challenging because of common degradations such as bleedthrough, faded ink, and stains. Achieving good binarization performance efficiently is important for extracting information from historical documents.
The paper proposes a recurrent neural network algorithm for image binarization using Grid Long Short-Term Memory cells, along with a pseudo F-Measure based weighted loss function.

The authors evaluate binarization and execution performance under different footprint sizes, scale factors, and loss functions. Experiments show significant trade-off between binarization time and quality for different footprint sizes, while different scale factors show no statistically significant difference.
The approach is compared with the best performing algorithm in the 2016 handwritten document image binarization contest, and both algorithms perform equally well.

The authors evaluate binarization and execution performance under different footprint sizes, scale factors, and loss functions. Experiments show no significant trade-off between binarization time and quality for different footprint sizes, while different scale factors show no statistically significant difference.
The paper argues that most text classification approaches model text only at the lexical and syntactic level, which limits domain robustness and explainability.
For sentiment analysis, lexical and syntactic approaches may have limited effectiveness when the texts consist of a series of arguments.
The paper claims that even a shallow model of a text's argumentation can support effective and robust classification while providing intuitive explanations of the classification results.

The authors apply this idea to supervised prediction of sentiment scores for reviews. They combine existing sentiment analysis methods with novel features that compare a review's argumentation structure to learned common sentiment flow patterns.
Evaluation in two domains demonstrates that modeling argumentation benefits text classification in both effectiveness and robustness.
The paper claims that even a shallow model of a text's argumentation can support effective and not robust classification while providing intuitive explanations of the classification results.
